submission.justification: After systematic simulation of all three candidate absorber materials across the allowed plate thickness range (2-10 mm), Absorber-F1 with 5.0 mm plates achieves the best energy resolution of 3.046% at 100 GeV. This represents a significant improvement over Absorber-F3 (3.756% at 4 mm) and Absorber-F2 (4.954% at 5 mm). The simulation tested multiple thickness values for each material, confirming that 5 mm is optimal for F1, balancing sampling frequency with shower containment. All candidate materials are documented as compatible with mechanical support and can be machined to required tolerances. This recommendation directly meets the primary goal of achieving the best possible energy resolution while satisfying all documented constraints.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F1 at 5mm achieves 3.046% resolution, the best among all tested configurations (F3: 3.756% at 4mm, F2: 4.954% at 5mm)

requirements.requirement: The absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F1 is explicitly listed as a candidate in candidate_specs.md as a dense alloy with short radiation length

requirements.requirement: The calorimeter must allow hands-on maintenance during shutdowns
requirements.evidence: All three materials are presented as viable candidates in the project documentation with no exclusions noted for maintenance accessibility. The requirement applies to the overall calorimeter design, which is compatible with all absorber options per meeting notes.
Recommended thickness of 5.0 mm is within the specified range of 2-10 mm
